title: Relative ampleness locus for a proper algebraic space
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $L$ be a line module on the small etale site of $X$ (an $\mathcal O_X$-module etale locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$). Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. There is an open subscheme $A\subset T$ such that, for every morphism $T'\to T$ of schemes, this morphism factors through $A$ if and only if $L_{T'}$ is relatively ample on $X_{T'}/T'$. Here relatively ample means that $X_{T'}$ is a scheme and that $L_{T'}$ restricts to an ample ordinary invertible module on the inverse image of every affine open of $T'$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Its points are exactly the $t$ for which $L$ on the geometric fibre $X_{\bar t}$ is ample; an ample line on an algebraic space over a field includes that this space is a scheme. Formation of $A$ commutes with arbitrary base change. In particular $X_A$ is a scheme, without a Noetherian or quasi-compact hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0D3D (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), including fibre criterion (A) in its proof; spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0D31 (definition-relatively-ample), which includes representability.

proof.text: Use the canonical ringed etale topoi of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] to interpret every pullback as $a^*L=\mathcal O\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O}a^{-1}L$. Such a pullback is still locally free of rank one: pull back a local trivialization and its inverse. Whenever its source is a scheme, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies it with an ordinary invertible module and identifies its tensor pullbacks with ordinary scheme pullbacks. We use this comparison throughout; thus every subsequent scheme ampleness lemma applies to the very same line module. The comparison is stated for every scheme morphism; the quasi-compact separated hypothesis in that node concerns only its direct-image clause, which is not used here.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, scheme interpretation of the invertible modules; descent.tex Tag 03DX supplies the explicit Zariski/etale comparison.

proof.text: First suppose $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ has image $t$ and the pulled-back line is ample on its schematic fibre. The map factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and gives a field extension $K/\kappa(t)$. By [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover] its spectrum is an fpqc cover. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent] to $X_t/\kappa(t)$ and this cover. It gives that $X_t$ is a scheme and $L_t$ is ample. Conversely ampleness on this schematic residue fibre persists after every field extension by [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change]. In particular the condition using one algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$ is equivalent to the condition using any field extension on which the fibre is ample.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, proof of (A), reduction from an arbitrary field to the residue field using 0D3C.

proof.text: Fix $t$ with $X_t$ a scheme and $L_t$ ample. Choose an affine open neighbourhood of $t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and temporarily replace $T$ by it and $X$ by its inverse image. This restriction is still proper: the diagonal and finite-type charts restrict, while every further base change is already a base change of the original universally closed morphism. The affine base is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-noetherian-approximation] to obtain $(X_i\to T_i)$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], since $T=\lim T_i$ is affine, on a tail all $T_i$ are affine schemes. The projections $X\to X_i$ and $T\to T_i$ are affine. No cartesianity of the approximation squares is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, proof of (A), proper approximation 0A0X followed by eventual affine bases 07SQ.

proof.text: The stages $X_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with affine transitions. Apply [lem-sfb-space-invertible-limit-descent] to $L$ on $X=\lim X_i$. After choosing an index and restricting to its tail there is a line $L_i$ on that stage; on later stages take its tensor pullbacks. They form a compatible system pulling back to $L$. Put $t_i$ equal to the image of $t$ in $T_i$.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, proof of (A), descent of the line module by 0D2X.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field], $\kappa(t)=\varinjlim_i\kappa(t_i)$. Thus $X_t=\varprojlim_i X_{i,t_i}$: on a test scheme $U$, a compatible tuple of maps to $X_{i,t_i}$ is a compatible tuple $U\to X_i$ together with compatible maps $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t_i)$ having equal composites to $T_i$. The two limits identify these with maps $U\to X$ and $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ having equal composites to $T$, which is exactly a map to $X_t$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], the fibre transition morphisms are affine. Indeed $X_{j,t_j}\to X_j\to X_i$ is affine (the first map is base change of a map of affine schemes), and it factors over the affine map $X_{i,t_i}\to X_i$. To check the resulting map is affine, take an affine scheme $U\to X_i$. Both $E=X_{j,t_j}\times_{X_i}U$ and $F=X_{i,t_i}\times_{X_i}U$ are affine schemes. The induced $E\to F$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]; its pullback to any affine scheme over $F$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Every affine test over $X_{i,t_i}$ factors through such an $F$ by its composite to $X_i$ (take $U$ to be that test). This verifies the space-affineness definition. The fibres are quasi-compact and separated, being proper finite-type fibres. Since $X_t$ is a scheme, [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] makes all $X_{i,t_i}$ schemes after a further tail. They now satisfy the scheme hypotheses of [lem-trf-ample-affine-limit-descent]; their limit is the scheme $X_t$ by the same universal property. Consequently $L_{i,t_i}$ is ample for some $i$.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, proof of (A), residue fields, schematic fibres 07SR, and ampleness descent 09MT.

proof.text: The scheme $T_i$ is Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is of finite presentation over $\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-ample-neighbourhood] to the proper $X_i\to T_i$ and its ample schematic fibre at $t_i$. Shrink the resulting neighbourhood to an affine $V_i\ni t_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Then $X_{i,V_i}$ is a scheme and $L_i$ is absolutely ample there. Let $V=T\times_{T_i}V_i$, an affine open neighbourhood of $t$ because $T\to T_i$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Its inverse image $X_V$ is the inverse image of $X_{i,V_i}$ under the affine projection $X\to X_i$, so it is a scheme and $X_V\to X_{i,V_i}$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible], $L_V$ is absolutely ample. For every affine open $W\subset V$, the map $X_W\to X_V$ is affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], being base change of the map between affine schemes $W\to V$; the same pullback lemma gives ampleness on $X_W$. This proves (A) with an affine relatively ample neighbourhood in the original $T$.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, last paragraph: 0D3A and affine pullback of an ample module (0892).

proof.text: Let $|A|$ be the set of $t\in T$ for which the geometric fibre is a scheme with ample line. Step 2 identifies these with the ample schematic residue fibres. Steps 3--6 give an open neighbourhood $V$ of each such $t$ on which $X_V$ is a scheme and $L_V$ is relatively ample. Conversely every point of such a $V$ has ample geometric fibre by [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change]. Hence $|A|$ is exactly the union of these opens. Equip it with its open subscheme structure. The family $\{V\to A\}$ is a jointly surjective etale family of schemes, and [lem-trf-algebraic-space-ample-local] applied to $X_A/A$ gives that $X_A$ is a scheme with relatively ample line. This glues over arbitrary open coverings; no finite cover or quasi-compactness of $A$ or $T$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D3D, (A) implies the lemma: construct the union and apply 0D36/0D3C to relative ampleness.

proof.text: Let $h:T'\to T$ be any scheme morphism. If it factors through $A$, base change of the relatively ample scheme family $X_A/A$ gives a scheme $X_{T'}$, and [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change] gives the required relative ampleness of $L_{T'}$. Conversely assume $X_{T'}$ is a scheme with relatively ample line. For every $t'\in T'$ the same base-change lemma gives ampleness of the fibre over $\kappa(t')$. Write $t=h(t')$; this fibre is $X_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t')$. By [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover] and [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent], $X_t$ is a scheme and $L_t$ is ample. Step 2 and the definition of $A$ give $t\in A$. Thus the image of $h$ lies in $A$, and $h$ factors uniquely through the open subscheme $A$: restrict the continuous map and its structure-sheaf homomorphism to this open target.

For a base change $T_1\to T$, the open $A_1=T_1\times_TA$ has the required universal property for $(X_{T_1},L_{T_1})$: a morphism $U\to T_1$ factors through $A_1$ exactly when its composite $U\to T$ factors through $A$, which by step 8 is exactly relative ampleness on $X_U/U$. Two open subschemes with this property contain one another, by applying it to their inclusion maps, so $A_1$ is the ample locus of the pulled-back family. Its geometric-fibre description is already that of step 7. Finally the inclusion $A\to T$ itself factors through $A$; step 8 yields that $X_A$ is a scheme. All these assertions use the established universal property and pullback identities only.
